extracted.intended_audience: general readers of The Muse interested in women's health, nonprofits, and public relations
extracted.subtask_short: writing news round-up about nonprofit PR
extracted.subtask_description: A short online news round-up summarizing a nonprofit controversy, explaining timeline/events, analyzing public-relations effects, and giving practical next steps for readers. Typically for an online magazine audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding exclusion for organizations under investigation
rubrics_metrics.description: A criteria that prevents the foundation from funding any organization currently under investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Komen cited this as the reason for withdrawing support from Planned Parenthood; the investigation in question was whether the organization is violating the law by using federal funds to pay for abortions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for funding direct-service providers
rubrics_metrics.description: Komen's stated preference to fund organizations providing direct service rather than organizations that only provide referrals (e.g., Planned Parenthood provides mammogram referrals but not mammograms).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Komen framed its reversal partly around the claim that it prefers to fund direct-service provision, not referral-only services; messaging about funding priorities should be explicit to avoid misunderstanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and transparency in explanation of decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizations should clearly explain the real reasons for funding decisions to avoid speculation and distrust (avoid vague language like 'misunderstanding').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Komen's initial wording and later statements (calling it a 'misunderstanding' and offering shifting explanations) intensified public suspicion; unclear explanations damage credibility and fuel speculation about hidden motives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain nonpartisan image to protect mission credibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Nonprofits associated with universally supported causes (e.g., fighting breast cancer) should avoid appearing to take political sides because doing so can harm broad support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article argues Komen's actions made it seem to have 'taken some sort of political side,' which likely caused 'irrevocable damage' to its image and alienated supporters across the political spectrum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider staffing and leadership optics
rubrics_metrics.description: Hiring leaders with known political stances (e.g., a 'staunch pro-lifer') affects public perception of organizational decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The recent hire of Komen executive Karen Handel (described as a staunch pro-lifer) contributed to suspicions about Komen's motives; organizations should weigh how leadership appointments will be perceived in context of policy decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure PR fallout by public engagement and donations
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess public-relations impact by monitoring social media backlash, supporters withdrawing allegiance, and shifts in donation flows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this case, social media exploded with dissatisfaction, long-time supporters announced loss of allegiance, and Planned Parenthood raised over $3 million in private donations—illustrating concrete metrics of PR damage and reputational loss.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crisis response: reversals and wording matter
rubrics_metrics.description: A public reversal of a controversial decision may not fully repair damage if the reversal's wording leaves uncertainty about future behavior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Komen announced it would be reversing its decision, but the phrasing left supporters unsure whether funding would actually continue—highlighting that how a reversal is communicated affects whether trust is restored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid letting political debates distract from core mission
rubrics_metrics.description: Leadership should prevent political controversies from diverting attention away from the organization's core mission (e.g., fighting breast cancer).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article notes Nancy Brinker's lament that debate is distracting from the Foundation’s real goal; organizations should proactively steer messaging back to mission and program impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Donor guidance: research and give directly to organizations you trust
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals who want to support women's health should bypass political debates by researching where donations go and giving directly to organizations they trust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical steps recommended: find organizations you support, do your research to find out where your money is really going, and if uncomfortable, find a different organization to back. The piece also points to resources ('Give Komen the Pink Slip: Five Ways to Support Women’s Health for All') for alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal health stewardship
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals should prioritize their own health through regular self-checkups and annual doctor appointments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article frames this as the most important action readers can take: 'make sure you’re caring for your own health... regular self-checkups and annual doctor’s appointments.' While not a PR rubric, it's presented as a concrete recommended action amid the controversy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informal 'score' of reputational outcome
rubrics_metrics.description: A simple evaluative summary comparing the parties based on outcome: Planned Parenthood gained public support and donations, Komen's reputation suffered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author summarizes: 'The score: Planned Parenthood: 1, Komen Foundation: Possibly in the negatives' — suggesting a quick heuristic for judging which side 'won' the PR/public-opinion battle.
